capabilities: Map notes and attachments on a folder-grouped grid
Draw arrows for links between files, including across folders
Search and filter files by name or path
Highlight and pin a file's connections
Open files in a split pane beside the graph
disambiguation: Not a kanban or task board; it draws a folder-grouped map of files and their links.
extras: Not distributed through the community plugin list: the README instructs building from source with Node.js 22 and copying main.js, manifest.json and styles.css into .obsidian/plugins/gridboard/. Interface available in eight languages; settings are shared across vaults in the same profile by default; no telemetry and works offline.
intentEvidence: an alternative to Obsidian’s built-in Graph view that maps your vault by folder
problem: Obsidian's Graph view arranges notes by link relationships, so it is hard to see how a project's files are laid out by folder.

relations.evidence: an alternative to Obsidian’s built-in Graph view that maps your vault by folder

summary: Folder-based graph view that places notes and attachments on a grid with a column per folder depth and arrows for links between files.
